post.summary:
AssumeUserIdentity exchanges the caller's cluster-admin credentials for
a Fuzzball user token bound to the target user inside the target
organization. The returned token's JWT carries an `act` claim
(RFC 8693) identifying the calling admin, so all downstream services
and audit records can attribute the action both to the impersonated
user (primary actor) and the impersonating admin (`impersonated_by`).

cluster (enforced by the WithRequireClusterAdmin auth wrapper).

posixGid.description: POSIX GID allocated to this group (0 = not yet allocated or LDAP-federated).

preemptIds.description:
Groups (by id) whose workflows this group is allowed to preempt.
Empty by default: this group's workflows preempt nothing.

fuzzball.api.v4.Account.description:
Account represents a group within an organization.
NOTE: The term "Account" is deprecated in favor of "Group". This message
represents a collaborative group of users within an organization, not to be
confused with user authentication credentials. The name remains "Account"
for backwards compatibility with existing API clients.

totalAccountUsers.title: total_account_users is the total number of users in the group

fuzzball.api.v4.AccountOwnerWorkflowsSum.description:
AccountOwnerWorkflowsSummary provides workflow statistics for group owners.
NOTE: "Account owner" refers to group owners (deprecated terminology).

AccountOwnerWorkflowsSummaryDetails provides detailed workflow info for group owners.
NOTE: "Account owner" refers to group owners (deprecated terminology).

fuzzball.api.v4.AccountRelationship.description:
AccountRelationship defines a user's role within a group.
NOTE: The term "Account" is deprecated. This enum represents group membership
relationships. Use GROUP_MEMBER and GROUP_OWNER when these values are added
in a future API version.

 - ACCOUNT_MEMBER: ACCOUNT_MEMBER indicates a user is a member of the group (deprecated, prefer GROUP_MEMBER)
 - GROUP_MEMBER: GROUP_MEMBER indicates a user is a member of the group
 - ACCOUNT_OWNER: ACCOUNT_OWNER indicates a user owns/administers the group (deprecated, prefer GROUP_OWNER)
 - GROUP_OWNER: GROUP_OWNER indicates a user owns/administers the group
 - ACCOUNT_ALL: ACCOUNT_ALL selects both owners and members (deprecated, prefer GROUP_ALL).
Used by list requests to return everyone regardless of role.
 - GROUP_ALL: GROUP_ALL selects both owners and members of the group.

priority.description: Scheduling priority for this group (organization owner only).

updatePriority.description: update_priority must be true for priority to be applied (presence flag).

updateName.description: update_name must be true for name to be applied (presence flag).

addPreemptIds.description: Group ids to add to this group's preemption list (organization owner only).

removePreemptIds.description: Group ids to remove from this group's preemption list (organization owner only).

workflowId.description: The workflow ID that is using the ref.

accountId.description:
The group (account) ID owning the ref. Set for group-namespace refs.
Exactly one of account_id / user_id identifies the owner, matching the ref.

userId.description:
The user ID owning the ref. Set for user-namespace refs.
Exactly one of account_id / user_id identifies the owner, matching the ref.

requireUpdatePassword.title: true = force password change on next login

generatedPassword.title: Only populated when password was auto-generated

clusterId.description:
cluster_id targets a specific orchestrate cluster when this request is
submitted to a federate cluster. The federate cluster forwards the
request to the named orchestrate, where the provisioner row is created
under the caller's federate organization. Ignored when the request is
submitted directly to an orchestrate cluster.

fuzzball.api.v4.AllocationQueue.description:
AllocationQueue identifies which scheduler queue an allocation sits in.
Mirrors the admin AdminAllocation.Queue values.

fuzzball.api.v4.AllocationStatus.description:
AllocationStatus is the job status of an allocation. Mirrors the admin
AdminAllocation.Status values.

fuzzball.api.v4.ApplicationOwnerKind.title:
- GROUP: default
 - ACCOUNT: deprecated alias for GROUP
 - ORGANIZATION: must be an organization owner to use
 - PROVIDER: only available via direct sql updates (for now)

organizationId.description:
organization_id is the customer organization (realm) hosting the
user to impersonate.

userId.description:
user_id is the target user. The minted token will be scoped to this
user's default account inside the organization.

jwt.description:
jwt is a Fuzzball-signed user token for the impersonated user. The
token has been processed through SelectAccount so it carries the
user's full identity context (POSIX uid/gid, group memberships) and
an `act` claim identifying the impersonating admin.

caCert.description: PEM-encoded CA certificate of the registering cluster.

category.title: if not provided a default will be set

storageProvisionerName.description:
Provisioner-backed volume creation (v4 path).
When set, creates a persistent volume on the named provisioner.

ownerUid.description: POSIX ownership for volume root directory (0 = use driver default).

permissions.description: POSIX file mode for volume root directory (e.g., 0755; 0 = use driver default).

ownerName.description:
Named user for volume ownership (resolved server-side to UID).
Mutually exclusive with owner_uid when non-empty.

ownerGroupName.description:
Named group for volume ownership (resolved server-side to GID).
Mutually exclusive with owner_gid when non-empty.

ownerUserUuid.description:
User UUID for volume ownership (resolved server-side to UID).
Mutually exclusive with owner_uid and owner_name when non-empty.

stages.description:
All stage rows matching the request; task arrays and multinode jobs have
one row per rank sharing a single allocation.

priority.description:
Set only for job and service stages whose allocation is still tracked by
the scheduler.

priorityUnavailableReason.description: Reason priority is absent for a job or service stage.

fuzzball.api.v4.DescribeWorkflowStageRes.description: DescribeWorkflowStageResponse is the response for the DescribeWorkflowStage RPC.

fuzzball.api.v4.ExplainAllocationReason.description:
ExplainAllocationReason mirrors the internal scheduler enum. Numbers 10-19
are reserved: 10 was PREEMPTION_INELIGIBLE in an earlier draft and has
been removed; 11-19 are held for Phase E fairshare variants. Do not reuse.

headShape.description:
head_shape is the resource shape of the reservation-holding (head)
allocation — the job being backfilled against.

blockingJobs.description:
blocking_jobs are the running jobs whose completion the backfill
reservation's estimated start is anchored on.

fuzzball.api.v4.ExplainBlockingJob.description:
ExplainBlockingJob identifies a running job whose completion the backfill
reservation's estimated start depends on.

token.description: Bearer token to present to the endpoint.

expiresAt.description: Absolute expiry time of the token.

url.description: The endpoint URL the token grants access to (convenience).

GetAccountOwnerWorkflowsSummaryDetailsResponse returns workflow details for group owners.
NOTE: "Account owner" refers to group owners (deprecated terminology).

GetAccountOwnerWorkflowsUsersResponse returns workflow users for group owners.
NOTE: "Account owner" refers to group owners (deprecated terminology).

fuzzball.api.v4.GetStageEventsResponse.description: GetStageEventsResponse is the response for the GetStageEvents RPC.

pageToken.description: Token to pass as page_token to fetch the next page; empty when no more.

fuzzball.api.v4.ListWorkflowsScope.title:
- SCOPE_USER: SCOPE_USER returns workflows for the user within the currently selected group
 - SCOPE_ACCOUNT: SCOPE_ACCOUNT returns workflows for the group (deprecated, prefer SCOPE_GROUP)

fuzzball.api.v4.MemberRelationship.description:
MemberRelationship identifies the role a user holds within a membership
listing (organization or group). It is only populated by member-listing
responses; it is left unspecified everywhere else a User is returned.

defaultTtlSeconds.description: Default TTL in seconds for objects in this scope.

id.description: The ID of the organization or group.

digest.description: The blob digest to point to.

ttlSeconds.title:
Optional TTL override in seconds.
- unset: inherit from hierarchy (group > org > cluster > system default)
- 0: no expiration (never purge)
- >0: explicit TTL in seconds

force.description:
Allow replacing an existing ref that points to a different digest.
When false (default), a request targeting an existing path whose content
differs is rejected with AlreadyExists; re-putting the identical digest
remains an idempotent no-op regardless of this flag.

ttlSeconds.description: Per-object TTL in seconds. Absent = inherited, 0 = no expiration, >0 = explicit.

effectiveTtl.description: Effective TTL after hierarchy resolution (vs the per-object override above).

options.title: list of options for the input

fuzzball.api.v4.OrganizationRelationship.description:
- ORGANIZATION_ALL: ORGANIZATION_ALL selects both owners and members. Used by list requests to
return everyone regardless of role.

requireUpdatePassword.description:
When true, the password is set as temporary and the user is required to change it on next login.
When false (default), the password is permanent and no forced change is required.

fuzzball.api.v4.QueueAllocationSummary.description:
QueueAllocationSummary is the user-facing view of a queued allocation. It
intentionally omits the owner/token/cluster-origin fields carried by the
admin AdminAllocationSummary: the owner is always the caller.

generatedPassword.title: Only populated when password was auto-generated

workflowId.description: The workflow ID releasing the ref.

accountId.description:
The group (account) ID owning the ref. Set for group-namespace refs.
Exactly one of account_id / user_id identifies the owner, matching the ref.

userId.description:
The user ID owning the ref. Set for user-namespace refs.
Exactly one of account_id / user_id identifies the owner, matching the ref.

clusterId.title: optional cluster ID when submitting jobs from a federate cluster

fuzzball.api.v4.SecretScope.description:
- SECRET_SCOPE_ACCOUNT: Deprecated: Use SECRET_SCOPE_GROUP instead.
 - SECRET_SCOPE_GROUP: SECRET_SCOPE_GROUP is the preferred name for group-scoped secrets (formerly SECRET_SCOPE_ACCOUNT).

id.description: The ID of the organization or group.

fuzzball.api.v4.StageEvent.description: StageEvent represents a single event in the lifecycle of a workflow stage.

fuzzball.api.v4.StageEventType.description:
StageEventType enumerates the types of events that can occur during stage execution.

 - STAGE_EVENT_TYPE_STAGE_STARTED: Stage lifecycle
 - STAGE_EVENT_TYPE_WORKFLOW_STARTED: Workflow lifecycle
 - STAGE_EVENT_TYPE_IMAGE_PULL_STARTED: Image pull events
 - STAGE_EVENT_TYPE_CONTAINER_STARTED: Container events
 - STAGE_EVENT_TYPE_SCALE_UP: Autoscaler emitted a persisted scale-up event for a service replica.
 - STAGE_EVENT_TYPE_SCALE_DOWN: A service replica was scaled down (stopped by the autoscaler/extension).
 - STAGE_EVENT_TYPE_WAITING_ON_DEPENDENCY: Dependencies
 - STAGE_EVENT_TYPE_RESOURCES_ALLOCATED: Resource allocation
 - STAGE_EVENT_TYPE_PROVISIONING_REQUESTED: Provisioning events
 - STAGE_EVENT_TYPE_VOLUME_CREATE_STARTED: Volume events
 - STAGE_EVENT_TYPE_FILE_TRANSFER_STARTED: File transfer events
 - STAGE_EVENT_TYPE_ERROR: Error
 - STAGE_EVENT_TYPE_PREEMPTED: Preemption events
 - STAGE_EVENT_TYPE_PRIORITY_SET: Priority events
 - STAGE_EVENT_TYPE_RESERVATION_HELD: Backfill events

effectivePriority.description:
effective_priority is only meaningful when computed is true; the
scheduler recomputes it each tick for ready and running allocations.

priorityExpression.description:
priority_expression is the cluster expression the scheduler evaluates;
the *_priority fields above and create_time are its inputs.

fuzzball.api.v4.StagePriorityDetails.description:
StagePriorityDetails reports the current scheduling priority of a job or
service stage and the inputs used to calculate it.

clusterId.title: optional cluster ID when submitting jobs from a federate cluster

applicationId.title: optional application ID to track application usage stats

preemptible.description:
preemptible indicates whether the workflow's allocations may be preempted
by higher priority allocations. Logically ORed with the definition's
top-level preemptible field; a job or service that sets preemptible
explicitly overrides the workflow-level value.

segment.description:
segment restricts this provisioner to nodes with a matching segment label.
If empty, the provisioner is globally accessible from any node.
Immutable after creation.

lustreCapacityGbs.description:
OCI Managed Lustre self-provisioning capacity in GB. OCI's minimum is
31200 GB (31.2 TB) across all tiers; valid sizes step by 10.4 TB up to
124.8 TB, then by 41.6 TB. 0 = use default.

lustrePerformanceTier.description:
OCI Managed Lustre performance tier in MBps per provisioned TB. One of
125, 250, 500, 1000. Empty = use default (125).

fuzzball.api.v4.StorageProvisionerStatus.description:
- STORAGE_PROVISIONER_STATUS_PROVISIONING: Self-provisioning of the backing cloud infrastructure (e.g. an OCI
Managed Lustre / FSS filesystem or AWS EFS) is in progress in the
background. The provisioner is not usable for volume operations until it
transitions to READY (or ERROR if provisioning failed).

sizeBytes.description: Volume capacity in bytes (0 = no change). Only set when --size is specified.

effectiveTtlSeconds.description: Effective TTL in seconds after hierarchy resolution.

fuzzball.api.v4.UpdateUserProfileSetting.description: TODO: given this is more of a backend support item we may want to remove this from the public api.

sizeBytes.description: Volume capacity in bytes (0 = no change). Only set when --size is specified.

fuzzball.api.v4.UpdateVolumeByNameReques.description: UpdateVolumeByNameRequest updates a volume identified by provisioner name + volume name.

fuzzball.api.v4.UsageStatsScope.title:
- USAGE_STATS_SCOPE_ALL: Usage across all accounts/organizations
 - USAGE_STATS_SCOPE_ACCOUNT: Usage within the user's account
 - USAGE_STATS_SCOPE_ORGANIZATION: Usage within the user's organization

fuzzball.api.v4.UserInfo.description: UserInfo is a lightweight user summary for embedding in other responses.

storageProvisionerId.description: Provisioner info (populated for provisioner-backed volumes, empty for class-based).

ownerUid.description: POSIX ownership and permissions for volume root (0 = driver default).

sizeBytes.description: Volume capacity in bytes (0 = unset/unlimited, driver-dependent).

createdBy.description:
UUID of the individual user who created this volume. For volumes
created before migration 000014 (which added the `created_by_user_id`
column), this field falls back to the group/account UUID for
backward compatibility — clients should treat such values as
pre-migration records whose individual creator is unrecoverable.

createdByName.description:
Email of the creating user, resolved via UserService. Empty for
pre-migration records where `created_by` is a group UUID that does
not resolve to a user.

fuzzball.api.v4.VolumeSource.description:
VolumeSource distinguishes volumes that Fuzzball provisioned from volumes
that exist outside Fuzzball. The orchestrate activity layer uses this to
decide whether create, chown, and delete operations are sent to the substrate.

UNSPECIFIED is treated as PROVISIONED so old clients and zero-valued fields
default to the Fuzzball-owned semantics.

reference.description:
Legacy v1/v3 volume URI ("volume://<scope>/<class>[/<name>]"). Retained for
backward compatibility with stored catalog values. New producers should set
storage_provisioner_name and volume_name instead.

storageProvisionerName.description:
v4 storage provisioner name (maps to a workflow volume's "use:" field).
Named to match the equivalent field on StorageVolume/VolumeInfoResponse.

volumeName.description: v4 persistent volume name (maps to a workflow volume's "name:" field).

accountId.title: account_id is the group ID this workflow belongs to (deprecated naming, represents a group)

version.description:
version defines the version of the workflow document.
Supported versions: "v1" (legacy reference-based volumes) and "v4" (provisioner-based volumes).

volumes.description:
volumes is a map defining volumes to use for this workflow by name.
Map keys define the name of the volume and values are specifications
detailing the data volume. Volume names are used by different
components of the workflow to reference a particular volume instance.

jobs.description:
jobs is a map defining jobs to run as a part of the workflow.
Map keys define the name of the job and values are specifications
detailing the compute job. Job names are used by different components
of the workflow to reference a particular compute job instance.

completed.description: TODO: Remove from public API as this is just an anchor for DAG execution.

annotations.title:
Annotations for the whole workflow. Currently, this is used by the
scheduler to place jobs in a certain topology zone

files.description:
files is a map defining files that may be injected into volumes and jobs.
Map keys define the name of the file and values are the file's contents.
Files names are used by job and volume.ingress components
to reference a specific file.

preemptible.description:
preemptible marks every allocation produced by this workflow (jobs,
services, and internal image/volume/file stages) as eligible for
preemption. Equivalent to `fuzzball workflow start --preemptible`.
An explicit per-job or per-service preemptible value overrides this
workflow-level setting.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.description:
WorkflowDefinition is the highest level unit of work for a Fuzzball cluster.
Workflows consist of orchestrating data volumes, container images and
container execution across a compute cluster.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Compl.description: TODO: Remove from public API as this is just an anchor for DAG execution.

service.description: service defines defaults that propagate to all services in the workflow.

env.description:
env is a list of environment variables to apply to both jobs and
services by default. Per-type defaults (job/service) and per-job or
per-service values take precedence.

mounts.description:
mounts is a map of default mounts to apply to both jobs and services.
Per-type defaults (job/service) and per-job or per-service mounts take
precedence.

resource.description:
resource specifies default resource requirements to apply to both jobs
and services. Per-type defaults (job/service) and per-job or per-service
resource values take precedence.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Defau.description:
Defaults defines workflow-level default settings applied to jobs and services.
Values can be overridden by per-type defaults (job/service) or by individual jobs/services.

env.description:
env is a list of environment variables to be exposed inside all job
containers.  Will be overridden by job level env variables.

mounts.description:
mounts is a map containing a key that references a volume by name and
value containing a specification with details of how that volume should
be mounted into the job container.

policy.description:
policy contains configurable rules that define high level execution
behavior of a job such as max execution time and retries on failure.

resource.description:
resource specifies the hardware requirements that must be met for the job
to be executed. This is used by the scheduler to determine if and where a
job can be scheduled to run.

volume.description:
volume specifies the volume name to mount at this path.
In path-keyed mount format, the map key is the mount path
and this field holds the volume name.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Defau.description:
Mount is the specification for how a volume gets mounted into a job
container.

cpu.description: cpu details CPU resource requirements for the job.

memory.description: memory details memory requirements for the job.

devices.description: device details device resource requirements for the job.

exclusive.description:
exclusive sets the requirement that this job is the only one running on
a node.

annotations.description:
annotations is a map of string key value pairs that can be used to
specify custom behavior implemented by the workflow system to meet
needs beyond what the first class resource parameters currently
provide. Potential use cases could be along the lines of:matching a job
to a specfic node pool, requiring a specific CPU microarchitecture or
GPU family, etc.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Defau.description:
Resource specifies hardware requirements that must be met for the
execution of a job.

affinity.description:
affinity dictates how the binding of tasks to the specific hardware
layout occurs. Must be one of "NUMA", "SOCKET", or "CORE". An unset
affinity defaults to "CORE".

cores.description: cores is the number of processor cores required.

threads.description:
threads dictates if hardware threads of allocated cores are exposed
to the job container.

sockets.description: sockets is the number of sockets required.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Defau.description: CPU contains relevant details about CPU requirements.

size.description:
size is the amount of memory required for the job. If no unit is
specified, byte is the default. E.g. 32KiB, 1GB, 32GiB.

byCore.description: by_core defines if the memory is specified per CPU core.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Defau.description: Memory contains relevant details about RAM requirements.

env.description:
env is a list of environment variables to be exposed inside all
service containers. Will be overridden by service level env variables.

mounts.description:
mounts is a map containing a key that references a volume by name and
value containing a specification with details of how that volume should
be mounted into the service container.

resource.description:
resource specifies the hardware requirements that must be met for the
service to be executed.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Defau.description:
Service defines defaults that propagate to all services in the workflow.
These defaults are applied to each service unless the service explicitly
sets a value for the same field. Services do not have a policy field, so
policy defaults are not supported here.

name.description:
Used internally to store the job name.  If this field is present in a
definition then it will be ignored in preference for the map key used in
the `jobs` field.

image.title:
Image is the URI to the container image to be used for this job.
Supported uri formats are: "docker://..." and "oras://" for OCI
and SIF(Singularity Image Format) images respectively.
E.g. docker://alpine:latest

command.description: command is the arguments executed by the container process.

env.description:
env is a list of environment variables to be exposed inside of the job
container.

mounts.description:
mounts is a map containing a key that references a volume by name and
value containing a specification with details of how that volume should
be mounted into the job container.

cwd.description:
cwd allows the specification of the the working dirctory used by the job.
This must be an absolute path. If unset the working directory defaults
first to the working directory in the OCI image config if present and
then to "/".

requires.description:
requires is a list of prerequisite jobs/services in the workflow that must be
completed before this job may be started. This allows jobs within a
workflow to be formed into a directed acyclic graph. If requirements
specified by different jobs results in a cycle, the workflow will fail to
start.

Deprecated: use the `dependsOn` field instead.
Ignored if `dependsOn` is set.
If used instead of `dependsOn`, dependencies are assumed to be "when jobN has finished".

policy.description:
policy contains configurable rules that define high level execution
behavior of a job such as max execution time and retries on failure.

resource.description:
resource specifies the hardware requirements that must be met for the job
to be executed. This is used by the scheduler to determine if and where a
job can be scheduled to run.

multinode.description: multinode enables a job to run across multiple nodes in parallel.

task-array.description:
task_array enables a job to be broken up into multiple tasks that run
concurrently. This is useful for doing embarrassingly parallel compute
work.

network.title: network defines if the job should run inside its own netowrk namespace

script.title: shebang script executed via command; if no "#!" line is present, "#!/bin/sh" is assumed

args.title: args passed to above script field, can also be passed to existing command

depends-on.description: dependsOn is a list of concrete dependencies that must be satisfied before this job can run.

preemptible.description:
preemptible marks this individual job as eligible for preemption.
When unset, the job inherits the workflow-level preemptible setting
(the top-level `preemptible` field or the --preemptible start flag).
An explicit true or false overrides the workflow-level setting.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Job.description:
Job is a single compute "step" in a workflow.
There are a variety of different types of jobs that
result in one or more containers being spawned.
By default, a single container is spawned unless the
TaskArray or Multinode fields are specified.

name.description: name is the name of the job to depend on.

status.title:
status is the status that this dependency must be in before this job can run.
Valid values (case-insensitive): RUNNING (Services Only), FINISHED

description.description: description is a human readable description of the dependency.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Job.D.description: Dependency is a concrete dependency that must be satisfied before this job can run.

volume.description:
volume specifies the volume name to mount at this path.
In path-keyed mount format, the map key is the mount path
and this field holds the volume name.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Job.M.description:
Mount is the specification for how a volume gets mounted into a job
container.

nodes.description: nodes is the number of nodes to run job across in parallel.

implementation.title:
implementation is the specific implementation of multinode to be used.
This must match the implementation used by the application within your
job container because different multinode implementations require
slightly different wire up configurations. Must be one of: "ompi",
"openmpi", "mpich", "gasnet", "generic"

procs-per-node.description:
procs_per_node specifies the number of processes to spawn
within each job container. If not specified, this value defaults to
the number of CPUs allocated to the job container. The total number
of processes spawned for a job can be calculated by multiplying
this value by the number of nodes requested.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Job.M.description:
Multinode enables a job to run multiple containers across multiple nodes
in parallel by leveraging various implementation for communication and
synchronization.

isolated.description:
isolated forces the use of a container network namespace.
This is required for reaching a job container port with port
forwarding.

expose-tcp.description: expose_tcp is a list of container TCP ports to expose.

expose-udp.description: expose_udp is a list of container UDP ports to expose.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Job.N.description:
Network defines if the job should be run inside its own network namespace
and enabled optional exposure of job container ports.
This is required if you want to expose ports from the job container
directly or via port forwarding.

cpu.description: cpu details CPU resource requirements for the job.

memory.description: memory details memory requirements for the job.

devices.description: device details device resource requirements for the job.

exclusive.description:
exclusive sets the requirement that this job is the only one running on
a node.

annotations.description:
annotations is a map of string key value pairs that can be used to
specify custom behavior implemented by the workflow system to meet
needs beyond what the first class resource parameters currently
provide. Potential use cases could be along the lines of:matching a job
to a specfic node pool, requiring a specific CPU microarchitecture or
GPU family, etc.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Job.R.description:
Resource specifies hardware requirements that must be met for the
execution of a job.

affinity.description:
affinity dictates how the binding of tasks to the specific hardware
layout occurs. Must be one of "NUMA", "SOCKET", or "CORE". An unset
affinity defaults to "CORE".

cores.description: cores is the number of processor cores required.

threads.description:
threads dictates if hardware threads of allocated cores are exposed
to the job container.

sockets.description: sockets is the number of sockets required.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Job.R.description: CPU contains relevant details about CPU requirements.

size.description:
size is the amount of memory required for the job. If no unit is
specified, byte is the default. E.g. 32KiB, 1GB, 32GiB.

byCore.description: by_core defines if the memory is specified per CPU core.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Job.R.description: Memory contains relevant details about RAM requirements.

start.description: start is the start of the range for Task ID values. Inclusive.

end.description: end is the end of the Task ID values. Inclusive.

concurrency.description:
concurrency is a limit on the number of tasks that can be run in
parallel. The max concurrency for a workflow job is 200.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Job.T.description:
TaskArray allows a job to be broken up in an embarrassingly parallel
manner for more effective execution. TaskArray jobs are automatically
populated with a `FB_TASK_ID` environment variable to indicate the index
within the task array range of the currently executing task to the
application.

timeout.description: timeout specifies rules related to the duration of a workflow step.

retry.description:
Deprecated: retry is not implemented and will be removed in a future
release. This field is accepted but ignored.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Polic.description:
Policy contains configurable rules for the execution of a workflow step.
The default policy for a step will set a value for timeout if a custom one
is not specified.

Deprecated: Retry is not implemented. This message will be removed in
a future release.

execute.description:
execute  is the maximum allowed duration of a workflow step to run
before it is failed.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Polic.description: Timeout specifies rules related to the duration of a workflow step.

exec.title: Probe action (exactly one must be specified)

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Probe.title: Probe defines Kubernetes-compatible health checking configuration
ExecAction represents a command-based probe (matches Kubernetes exactly)
GRPCAction represents a gRPC probe (matches Kubernetes exactly)
HTTPGetAction represents an HTTP GET probe (matches Kubernetes exactly)
HTTPHeader represents an HTTP header for HTTP probes (matches Kubernetes exactly)
TCPSocketAction represents a TCP socket probe (matches Kubernetes exactly)

name.description:
Used internally to store the job name.  If this field is present in a
definition then it will be ignored in preference for the map key used in
the `jobs` field.

image.title:
Image is the URI to the container image to be used for this job.
Supported uri formats are: "docker://..." and "oras://" for OCI
and SIF(Singularity Image Format) images respectively.
E.g. docker://alpine:latest

command.description: command is the arguments executed by the container process.

env.description:
env is a list of environment variables to be exposed inside of the job
container.

mounts.description:
mounts is a map containing a key that references a volume by name and
value containing a specification with details of how that volume should
be mounted into the job container.

cwd.description:
cwd allows the specification of the the working dirctory used by the job.
This must be an absolute path. If unset the working directory defaults
first to the working directory in the OCI image config if present and
then to "/".

requires.description:
requires is a list of prerequisite jobs/services in the workflow that must be
completed before this service may be started. This allows jobs within a
workflow to be formed into a directed acyclic graph. If requirements
specified by different jobs results in a cycle, the workflow will fail to
start.

Deprecated: use the `dependsOn` field instead.
Ignored if `dependsOn` is set.
If used instead of `dependsOn`, dependencies are assumed to be "when jobN has finished".

resource.description:
resource specifies the hardware requirements that must be met for the job
to be executed. This is used by the scheduler to determine if and where a
job can be scheduled to run.

multinode.description: multinode enables a service to run across multiple nodes in parallel.

script.title: shebang script executed via command; if no "#!" line is present, "#!/bin/sh" is assumed

args.title: args passed to above script field, can also be passed to existing command

depends-on.description: dependsOn is a list of concrete dependencies that must be satisfied before this service can run.

persist.description:
defines if the service should run even if there are no running or waiting jobs in the workflow.
If persist is set to false, the service is stopped when all dependant jobs and services have stopped.
If persist is set to true, the service runs even if there are no dependant jobs/services and continues until the workflow is cancelled.

readiness-probe.title: readinessProbe controls the STARTED → RUNNING transition of the service (required for proper lifecycle monitoring)

autoscaler.description: autoscaler configures automatic scaling for this service.

dynamic-config.description:
dynamic_config injects a dynamically-rendered config file into the
service container, updated as referenced services' addresses change.

preemptible.description:
preemptible marks this individual service as eligible for preemption.
When unset, the service inherits the workflow-level preemptible setting
(the top-level `preemptible` field or the --preemptible start flag).
An explicit true or false overrides the workflow-level setting.

replicas.description:
replicas bounds the replica count for this service. Mutually exclusive
with scale_up triggers that target other services (`triggers[].services`).

scale-up.description: scale_up lists the triggers that add replicas (including from zero).

scale-down.description: scale_down policy removes replicas of this service.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Servi.description:
Autoscaler enables automatic scaling of this service's replicas, or, when
a scale_up trigger sets `services`, emission of scale events for other
services.

enabled.description: enabled turns on metrics collection for the service.

path.description: path is the HTTP path to the service metrics endpoint.

port.description: port is the service container port exposing the metrics endpoint.

interval.description: interval is the scrape interval in seconds.

includes.description:
includes restricts collection to the named metrics; all metrics are
collected when empty.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Servi.description: Metrics configures collection of service metrics used by scale policies.

min.description: min is the minimum number of replicas (0 enables scale-to-zero).

max.description: max is the maximum number of replicas.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Servi.description: Replicas bounds the number of replicas for an autoscaled service.

metrics-query.description:
metrics_query is a PromQL expression evaluated against collected
metrics; a true (non-zero) result triggers the scaling action.

cooldown-period.description:
cooldown_period is the minimum number of seconds between consecutive
scaling actions.

services.description:
services lists the services this policy scales instead of the owning
service. Only valid on a scale_up trigger (cross-service bootstrap from
zero): the trigger then emits one event per target service, and the
owning service must not define replicas. Leave empty to scale the
owning service itself. Must not be set on scale_down.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Servi.description: ScalePolicy defines a PromQL query and cooldown for a scaling action.

triggers.description:
triggers are the independent scale-up conditions, each with its own
query, targets, and cooldown.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Servi.description:
ScaleUp is the set of scale-up triggers. Each trigger independently
evaluates its metrics-query (scoped per replica) and, when it fires,
scales its target services — or this service's own replicas when the
trigger sets no services. All triggers of a service must agree: either
every trigger targets other services (cross-service source), or none do
(self-scaling pool).

path.description: path is the destination path of the rendered file inside the container.

services.description:
services lists the services whose addresses are made available to the
script (e.g. service "worker" is exposed as the SERVICES_WORKER array).

script.description:
script is a bash script executed in a restricted interpreter (builtins
only, no command execution or file I/O) whose stdout becomes the file
contents.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Servi.description:
DynamicConfig renders a config file from the live IP addresses of other
services and injects it into this service's container.

endpoints.description: Configures fuzzball endpoints to expose a service's functionality.

host.title: Service serves on the host network

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Servi.description:
Network defines if the job should be run inside its own network namespace
and enabled optional exposure of job container ports.
This is required if you want to expose ports from the job container
directly or via port forwarding.

port-name.description: The name of the port defined above to proxy to.

protocol.title:
The endpoint's intended protocol.
Valid values are: http, https, grpc, grpcs, tcp, tls

type.title:
The type of endpoint to create.
Valid values are: subdomain, path
subdomain - creates a subdomain endpoint like myservice.workflow_id.account_id.fuzzball
path - creates a path based endpoint like /endpoints/account_id/workflow_id/myservice

scope.title:
The scope defines who can access this endpoint.
Valid values are: user, group, organization, public
user - only the workflow creator can access
group - anyone in the same account can access
organization - anyone in the same organization can access
public - no authentication required
Default: group (if not specified)

name.description: The name used to refer to this port.

port.description: The port number exposed by the service container.

protocol.title: The protocol used by this port. Valid values are: tcp, udp

uri.description: uri is the uri of the resource to be accessed.

secrets.description:
secrets is a map of key value pairs to use to access resource.
The key specifies the type of data that is being used and the value
specifies raw data or a template for the workflow system to populate with
data internally from the secrets engine.

cache.title:
cache controls ingress caching behavior for this source URI.
Valid values (case-insensitive): once, changed, never

cache-ttl.description:
cache_ttl_seconds sets a custom TTL for auto-cached ingress objects.
If unset (0), defaults to 7 days.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.URI.description:
URI contains the specification for a resource to access as well as
additional data necessary for access such as credentials.

name.description:
Name is the key value of the volume in the volume map containing this
struct. This is normally set internally by client side code when parsing
workflow DSLs, but will need to be set when calling the API directly.

type.title:
type is the kind of volume. This currently determines the lifetime of the
volume and the data contained within it.
Ephemeral volumes are empty upon creation and have a lifespan of the
workflow duration. Upon workflow completion the volume and its data are
deleted. Host volumes represent directories on the shared filesystems of
the nodes themselves. They must be pre-existing and fall under
directories specified in the shared-fs-roots config property of the
Volume service. Must be one of "EPHEMERAL" or "HOST".
Deprecated in favor of reference

ingress.description:
Ingress specifies data that should be fetched and made available within
the volume.

egress.description:
Egress specifies data that exists within the volume that should be
exported to another storage location.

path.title:
Path is specified for host volume types with the absolute path to the
directory to mount.
Deprecated: will be removed

reference.description: Volume reference this volume is referring to.

use.description:
use specifies the storage provisioner name, "ephemeral", or "persistent".
When set, this replaces the legacy reference-based volume resolution.

size.description: size is the requested volume capacity (e.g. "10GB", "1TiB").

annotations.description: annotations is a map of key-value pairs used for provisioner auto-selection.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Volum.description:
Volume is an instance of a data volume used within the scope of a workflow.
There are a couple different types of volumes that have different data
retention behavior. Volumes are the means of managing data for compute
applications to process over the course of a workflow and orchestrate
data movement to bring injest data into the bounds of a workflow for
computation or export data generated from computation it to other storage
locations.

TODO(cedric): deprecate type/path fields
 reserved 2, 5;
 reserved "type", "path";

source.description:
Source is the origin of the data. The type of URIs supported are
determined by whether this is specified under ingress or egress.

destination.description:
Destination is the location to move the data. The type of URIs
supported are determined by whether this is specified under ingress or
egress.

policy.description:
policy contains configurable rules that define high level execution
behavior of a data transfer such as max execution time and retries on
failure.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Volum.description: File specifies details of workflow volume data movement.

serviceName.description: Service (from the workflow definition) exposing the endpoint.

endpointName.description: Endpoint name (from the service network definition).

url.description: Fully-qualified URL clients use to reach the endpoint.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowEndpoint.description:
WorkflowEndpoint is a live workflow service endpoint exposed through the
Fuzzball service proxy.

expirationSeconds.description: Token lifetime in seconds. 0 selects the server default.

name.description: Name of the container to execute the command in.

rank.description: Rank of the container to execute the command in.

name.description: Name of the container to execute the command in.

rank.description: Rank of the container to execute the command in.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowStatus.description:
- STAGE_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED: also used for pending
 - STAGE_STATUS_DOWN: STAGE_STATUS_DOWN marks an autoscaled service replica that has been scaled down.

numa-node.description: Numa node associated to the device.

allocated.title:
Is the device allocated, only used for fuzzball.substrate.api.substrate.v1.ResourceShowResponse,
this field is ignored when set by a plugin returning DeviceInitResponse

hardwareThreads.title: list of hardware threads of the core (nil for threads)

socketPackage.title: socket package associated to the core

numaNode.title: NUMA node associated to the core

cores.title: list of CPU cores on a system

freeCores.title: number of free CPU cores (hardware threads are not accounted)

memoryTotalBytes.title: total memory available on a system

memoryFreeBytes.title: free memory available on a system

memoryBytesByCore.title: rough estimation of the amount of memory available by CPU core

numaNodes.title: NUMA nodes available on a system

cores.title: list of CPU cores associated to a NUMA node

freeCores.title: number of free CPU cores (hardware threads are not accounted)

memoryTotalBytes.title: total memory available on a NUMA node

memoryFreeBytes.title: free memory available on a NUMA node

memoryBytesByCore.title: rough estimation of the amount of memory available by CPU core

total.description: total is the total available resource on the compute service.

free.description: free is the currently free resource on the compute service.

node.description: node is the detailed node information of the compute service.

annotations.description: annotations is the list of annotations associated with the node.

cores.title: list of CPU cores associated to a socket

freeCores.title: number of free CPU cores (hardware threads are not accounted)

numaNodes.title: list of NUMA nodes associated to a socket

google.protobuf.NullValue.description:
`NullValue` is a singleton enumeration to represent the null value for the
`Value` type union.

The JSON representation for `NullValue` is JSON `null`.

 - NULL_VALUE: Null value.
